s8.title: 4414 HighTide | Behind the Bumpers | REBUILT Champions

bet.text: Capacity, throughput and a turret to go around defense: the team believed these matter most at the highest level of play.

demand.text: Fuel scoring and passing. The team made it able to shoot on the bump while under defense, and added a hood roller because the static hood could not shoot or pass very far.

auto.text: Autos are states that drive to points. Side cameras give a position as the robot crosses the bump, until the main Limelight can see tags.
When no partner took the outpost, an analyst saw one pass through the middle, a push along the hub wall, then scoring from the outpost.

cycle.text: Intaking balls fill the robot from the rear and stay loosely packed, so it can shoot without gaps.
At Orange County an analyst saw it take opponents' fuel outside its shift, wait without collecting more, then go back to the middle for fuel it had just scored.

endgame.text: At Orange County an analyst saw it score from on the bump in the last seconds, after its alliance had left little fuel on its own side for the endgame.

fallback.text: After its alliance lost auto in Einstein finals 1, an analyst says it cleared the neutral zone during the transition shift instead of going back to score. The alliance lost that match with a partner disabled.

gave_up.text: Chamfered corners needed custom swerve plates, and the dye rotor forced a split drive rail with a tight battery fit. The flexible net could hide the tags from the main Limelight when full. Hood roller belts took much of the space for flywheel mass.

changed.text: The static hood used at Orange County and the district championship took a lot of current and could not shoot very far, so a hood roller was added before the world championship. So were two side cameras. The net, first zip-tied to the turret's top plate, got a slotted metal plate. The binder shows 10 rotor and 11 shooter versions.

outcome.text: 70-2-0 in official play; won the Daly division, won the championship; captain of the Daly alliance on Einstein; ranked 1 of the pooled top 20 (OPR 429.48, Daly).

solves.text: Maximize hopper area and dye rotor diameter within the frame perimeter, with the rotor kept low

facts.text: Frame size 25 x 32 in
Two custom swerve modules use WCP Swerve X2 components
The only custom module parts are three milled aluminum plates
Swerve gearing 7.67:1, to minimize current draw when accelerating
The left drive rail is split to move the battery to the edge; two cross rails provide structure to the dye rotor

cost.text: The battery is a very tight fit and needed some custom work; the team reported no problems with it

functions.name: Bumpers
functions.type: structural bumpers that form the hopper walls

solves.text: Gain hopper space and support the shooter with the bumper backing

facts.text: Extra hopper space per side, about
Mainly .090 in bent aluminum, with bent polycarbonate side panels reinforced with SRPP
3D printed stadium pieces funnel balls into the dye rotor
Only the bumpers and the dye rotor sit between the shooter and the robot, so the turret is somewhat free spinning when the bumpers are off

functions.name: Intake
functions.type: linear extending roller intake with independent sides

solves.text: Survive impacts by collapsing at once, with no crash bar

facts.text: Primary 3 in polycarbonate roller powered by two Kraken X60s at 3.45:1
Bottom 1.5 in roller powered by one Kraken X44 at 1.5:1
The bottom roller is stored behind the front roller, drops on surgical tubing at the start of the match and is held by latches
Doubled .25 in polycarbonate gear racks act as leaf springs, with one Kraken X44 on each side
Each side slides independently and springs back out after a hit

functions.name: Extending hopper and net
functions.type: extending hopper with a flexible net

solves.text: Add capacity while the starting configuration stays under the trench

facts.text: Holds under the trench, at least
Holds over the bump with the net, at least
A season reviewer gives its hopper as 80 fuel
A slotted metal plate holds the net, and a plate below guards the turret gear

cost.text: When full, the net could block the main Limelight's view of the hub tags, so two side cameras were added before the world championship

functions.name: Dye Rotor
functions.type: coaxially powered dye rotor with passive rollers

solves.text: Feed the shooter without jams or gaps

facts.text: Two Kraken X60s drive the rollers, with 2.5:1 on the feeder wheels, and one rotates the rotor at 36.4:1
Powered coaxially through a long belt and a reinforced gear train, not through a slip ring
Passive rollers let each ball push the one ahead up the tunnel and lower current draw
The vertical wheel sits inside the rotor, so balls settle in front of it with zero compression
A dolphin fin ramp on the outside of the slowly reversing rotor agitates balls and reduces packing pressure
A commenter says it indexed more slowly than 4946 but performed far better because it was short

functions.name: Shooter
functions.type: geared flywheel with a powered hood roller

solves.text: Recover speed fast and shoot far from a compact turret

facts.text: Four Kraken X44s geared 1:1 to a 3 in flywheel
Three 1 in feeder wheels with .5 in compression, and a 1 in hood roller at half the surface speed
Every wheel in the shooter is geared together
Copper flywheels .25 in thick, plus copper discs inside the wheels
Two GT2 belts over the hood side plates drive the hood roller
Hood driven by one Kraken X44 at 85.3:1
All motors are stacked vertically so few parts protrude

functions.name: Turret
functions.type: compact turret on an X-contact bearing

solves.text: Go around defense, in little height

facts.text: One Kraken X44 at 55.7:1
The X-contact bearing is shared by the dye rotor and the shooter
A sliding flex-wheel tensioner with two 8 lb constant force springs takes up the cable chain
Height of the turret and cable chain stack-up, less than

functions.name: Software
functions.type: precomputed shot map with tilt compensation

solves.text: Shoot and feed while moving, tilted or under defense

facts.text: For a range of distances and robot velocities it computes all possible scoring shots beforehand and finds the one most robust to errors
Shots simulated in one sweep for the hub, about
A second-order polynomial looks up hood angle and flywheel speed at runtime; the turret compensates for tangential velocity
Robot pitch and yaw correct the shot so it can shoot on the bump
One Limelight that always points at the hub does about 95 percent of localization; two side cameras help when it cannot see tags
Fully state-machine based, with no commands

decisions.because: iteration found it the most consistent and accurate setup, which surprised the team
decisions.instead_of: an independent feeder that regulates speed before the flywheel

decisions.choice: Change from command-based code to state machines
decisions.because: command-based code caused loop overruns and was harder to debug

decisions.choice: Add a hood roller between the district and world championships
decisions.because: the static hood took a lot of current and could not shoot or pass very far
decisions.cost: its belts took space for flywheel inertia

decisions.because: the hood roller belts left little space and copper is slightly denser than steel

decisions.choice: Chamfer the back corners with custom swerve modules
decisions.because: balls pack better than in square corners and the drive base is larger for the same perimeter
decisions.cost: custom module plates and difficult packaging around the dye rotor

decisions.choice: Extend the bumpers into hopper walls
decisions.because: newer bumper rules allow about an inch and a half of hard parts beyond the frame, and a dye rotor can use extra space on three sides

decisions.choice: Thick polycarbonate front roller with no crash bar
decisions.because: it needs no sacrificial material in front and helps compliance

decisions.choice: Cut the turret gear at 20 DP
decisions.because: it doubles the ratio available compared with 10 DP, so the gearbox is compact

decisions.choice: Write fully state-machine code with no commands
decisions.because: it is easier to reason about for the AI agents that attempt features, which people review
